sources.name: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5 / ERA5-Land reanalysis)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (Open-Meteo); ERA5 contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information
sources.spatialResolution: ERA5 ~25 km / ERA5-Land ~9 km grid; one point per division (divisional HQ)
sources.notes: Reanalysis, not station observations — labelled Historical. Daily precipitation, temperature, FAO-56 ET0 and 0-7 cm soil moisture from 1991-01-01.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Forecast API
sources.spatialResolution: best-match NWP models, 1-11 km; one point per division or a chosen location
sources.temporalResolution: daily (7 past + 16 forecast days); hourly soil moisture
sources.notes: Third-party weather forecast — labelled Predicted. Used by the Smart Irrigation Advisor and the 30-day rainfall KPI.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Flood API (GloFAS v4 river discharge reanalysis)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (Open-Meteo); GloFAS © Copernicus Emergency Management Service
sources.spatialResolution: 0.05° grid cells on the Ganges, Brahmaputra-Jamuna and Upper Meghna
sources.notes: Modelled discharge, used only for the monthly shape of transboundary inflow (not for volumes).

sources.name: FAO AQUASTAT Dissemination System
sources.temporalResolution: annual; many Bangladesh values are 2008 or 2018 figures carried forward by AQUASTAT
sources.notes: Renewable resources, withdrawals by sector, irrigated areas, environmental flow requirement. Division splits made by AquaGuard are Estimated.

sources.name: CSR GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06.3 Mascon Solutions (all corrections)
sources.license: Free to use with citation: Save, H., Bettadpur, S., Tapley, B.D. (2016) JGR Solid Earth, doi:10.1002/2016JB013007; Save, H. (2020) doi:10.15781/cgq9-nh24
sources.notes: Terrestrial water storage anomaly (cm equivalent water height) averaged over Bangladesh. Regional storage trend only — not well depth or water level.

sources.name: geoBoundaries (gbOpen) — Bangladesh ADM0/ADM1/ADM2
sources.license: ADM1: CC0 1.0; ADM2: CC BY 3.0 IGO (source BBS, OCHA ROAP)
sources.spatialResolution: simplified polygons (further simplified by AquaGuard, ~300 m tolerance)
sources.notes: Runfola et al. (2020) geoBoundaries, PLoS ONE 15(4): e0231866. Areas computed by AquaGuard are Estimated.

sources.name: HDX COD-PS Bangladesh subnational population statistics 2022
sources.notes: Used for domestic demand and population-weighted splits.

sources.name: World Bank Population Estimates and Projections (SP.POP.TOTL, source 40)
sources.notes: Projected years are third-party projections; AquaGuard's demand projection using them is labelled Estimated (projection).

sources.name: Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) station data — CSV importer
sources.license: Subject to BWDB terms; data must be requested/registered
sources.notes: Not bundled. Drop CSV files matching docs/DATA_SOURCES.md#bwdb into data/raw/bwdb/ and run ml/import_bwdb.py; records are stored as Observed.

sources.name: JRC Global Surface Water — occurrence (1984-2021)
sources.license: Free of charge, attribution required: Pekel et al. (2016) Nature 540, 418-422 (EC JRC / Google)
sources.notes: Displayed as raster map tiles in the 3D Water Explorer, loaded directly by the browser.

sources.name: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (Terrarium encoding)
sources.notes: 3D terrain (raster-dem). Bangladesh is mostly flat; vertical exaggeration is labelled on the map.

sources.name: CARTO Positron basemap (OpenStreetMap data)
sources.license: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), © CARTO; free for non-commercial use under CARTO's terms
sources.notes: Base map only; rivers and canals shown come from the OpenStreetMap-based basemap labels and waterway layer.

sources.name: AquaGuard engines (water balance, FAO-56, scenario, flow simulation)
sources.notes: Calculated values are Estimated; scenario and network outputs are Simulated.

sources.name: AquaGuard ML pipeline (climatic water balance forecasts)
sources.notes: Trained offline (make ml); metrics read from ml/artifacts/metrics.json.

parameters.source: Derived: FAO AQUASTAT 'Surface water produced internally' (83.91 km3/yr, var 4155) / 'Long-term average annual precipitation in volume' (393.42 km3/yr, var 4150), reference year 2018
parameters.note: National ratio applied uniformly to every division (assumption A-04).

parameters.source: Derived: FAO AQUASTAT 'Environmental Flow Requirements' (600.3 km3/yr, var 4549) / 'Total renewable surface water' (1205.91 km3/yr, var 4185), reference year 2018
Derived: FAO AQUASTAT 'Municipal water withdrawal per capita (total population)' 20.995 m3/inhab/yr (var 4457) x 1000 / 365
FAO AQUASTAT 'Industrial water withdrawal' 0.77 km3/yr (var 4252), last non-imputed year 2008
parameters.note: Split to divisions by 2022 population share (assumption A-06).

parameters.source: FAO AQUASTAT 'Surface water: total external renewable' 1122 km3/yr (var 4176), reference year 2018
parameters.note: Split to divisions by area share (assumption A-05); monthly shape from GloFAS discharge.

parameters.source: FAO AQUASTAT 'Total renewable groundwater' 21.122 km3/yr (var 4187), reference year 2018
parameters.note: Split by area share; usable in any month in proportion to monthly demand (aquifer storage buffer, assumption A-07).

parameters.source: Assumption — no national distribution-loss statistic in AquaGuard's sources. Replace with utility non-revenue-water data.
parameters.note: Applied to piped domestic and industrial conveyance. Irrigation losses are inside irrigation_efficiency.
